title: Docker Compose for Local Data Stacks

scenes.heading: Docker Compose for Local Data Stacks
scenes.subheading: Spin up a whole stack with one command
scenes.narration: Docker Compose lets you define and run a multi-service data stack with a single declarative file.

scenes.heading: What Compose gives you
bullets: Define many services in one YAML file
Networking between services out of the box
One command to start and stop everything
scenes.narration: Compose lets you describe every service your stack needs in one YAML file. It wires those services onto a shared network automatically so they can reach each other by name. Named volumes keep your database data alive between restarts. And a single command brings the whole environment up or tears it down.

scenes.heading: A local data stack
scenes.code:
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: devpass
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  airflow:
    image: apache/airflow:2.9.0
    depends_on:
      - postgres
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"

volumes:
  pgdata:
scenes.narration: This file declares two services, a Postgres database and an Airflow scheduler. The database exposes its port and stores data in a named volume so nothing is lost on restart. The Airflow service declares a dependency on Postgres so it starts in the right order, and exposes its web interface on port eight thousand eighty.

scenes.heading: The Compose workflow
scenes.narration: You author the compose file once to describe your stack. Bringing it up starts every service together for local development. When you are finished, bringing it down cleanly stops and removes the containers while preserving your named volumes.

scenes.text: Compose is perfect for reproducible local dev and testing, but reach for Kubernetes when you run in production.
scenes.narration: Use Compose for reproducible local development and testing, and graduate to Kubernetes when you need to run these workloads in production at scale.
